note: Credit pricing for AI features. Nothing here charges anybody: Stage 6 prepares the meter, it does not switch it on. Enforcement is off in ai-config.js (billing.enforce) and this file is read to COUNT, not to bill. Prices live here rather than in code so a tier or a feature price is a data edit — and so that when this moves to Postgres it moves as rows, not as a deploy. See docs/ai-roadmap.md.

classifyProject.note: A short structured prompt and a short JSON answer. Measured against the real prompt in proxy/worker.js, not guessed.

generateImage.note: Not implemented. Priced now so the meter is not redesigned when it is — an image is roughly an order of magnitude more expensive than a classification.

generateSchematic.note: Not implemented. A long reasoning task with a long structured answer.

generateModel.note: Not implemented. The most expensive thing on the roadmap, and priced to say so.

multiplierNote: Zero is a real price, not a missing one. The rules, the cache and an on-device model cost nothing to run, so they must cost nothing to use — otherwise a client on a small plan is pushed towards the expensive answer by their own allowance, which is exactly backwards.

plans.note: Everything that runs on a free tier or on the client's own device. No paid provider, so this plan cannot generate a bill.
Blocks at the allowance rather than charging past it. A surprise invoice is a worse experience than a feature that stops.
Keeps working past the allowance and flags it, for a client whose work must not stop mid-job. 'notify' still needs somewhere to notify — see docs/ai-roadmap.md.

overageNote: 'block' stops at the allowance. 'notify' continues and marks the usage. There is deliberately no 'charge' option yet: metering that bills is a different kind of system, and it is not this one.
